title: Baggage Allowance and Duty Exemption
summary: The baggage allowance policy for passengers arriving by land has evolved from a fixed $300 USD exemption to $400 USD, with the introduction of frequency limits (max 3 times per calendar year) to prevent abuse. The regulatory framework consistently maintains provisions for duty-free clearance for specific categories, including deceased persons and medical equipment for vulnerable passengers, and has been updated in 2025 to standardize declaration processes.

evolution.eligibility_constraints: Introduced annual frequency caps to regulate usage.
evolution.structure: Standardized the declaration process and duty-free lists.

timeline.change: Established $300 USD duty-free allowance for land passengers.
Maintained $300 limit; added specific duty exemption for deceased persons.
Increased land passenger allowance to $400 USD.
Added frequency limit of 3 times per calendar year.
Maintained $400 limit and frequency cap; added specific exemption for medical equipment for sick/disabled/elderly.
Defined duty-free limits for land-based passengers and adjudication procedures for excess baggage.

Passenger Baggage Allowance: This clause outlines the conditions for importing goods that exceed the standard baggage allowance or categories defined in the relevant schedules.
Passengers may import items outside the specified schedules, provided the goods are not restricted or prohibited under import policy orders or other applicable laws.
The release of such goods is contingent upon the presentation of a clearance certificate from the Chief Controller of Imports and Exports.
The goods may be cleared only after undergoing the Adjudication of Customs Offences process, which includes the payment of all applicable duties, taxes, fines, and penalties.
Adjudication of Customs Offences: This process is mandated for the clearance of baggage goods that exceed specified schedules or limits.
It serves as the legal mechanism to determine and collect the required duties, taxes, and any associated fines or penalties before the release of non-standard baggage imports.
Chief Controller of Imports and Exports: The entity is designated as the authority whose clearance certificate must be obtained and presented by a passenger to import goods outside of the permitted baggage schedules.

It requires passengers to provide personal details, travel history, and information on whether they are carrying specific categories of restricted or dutiable items.
Schedule: The form references specific schedules that categorize goods for the purpose of customs assessment and duty-free allowances.
Schedule-2: Schedule-2 specifies goods that are subject to customs duty and taxes, requiring passengers to declare if they are carrying more than the prescribed quantity.
Schedule-3: Schedule-3 lists goods that are eligible for duty-free entry, with specific quantitative limits defined for items like mobile phones.
Red Channel: The Red Channel is the designated clearance area where passengers must report to a customs officer if they are carrying dutiable, prohibited, or excess quantity items as indicated in their baggage declaration.
Customs Officer: Customs officers are responsible for receiving declarations from passengers at the Red Channel and verifying the imported goods against the declared items.
Gold and Silver Bullion: Specific declaration requirements apply to gold and silver bars, bullion, and ornaments based on their weight and frequency of import.
Revenue Officer: The Revenue Officer is the designated official authorized to validate the baggage declaration process.
